title: Cofibrant inclusion gives an equivalence of coherent localizations
statement:
Use model categories, weak equivalences, cofibrant objects and functorial factorizations as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and homotopy coherent localization with its full functor-category universal property as in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Enlarge universes to contain the nerves and localizations below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category, let $\mathcal M^c$ be its full ordinary subcategory of cofibrant objects, and give this subcategory the weak equivalences $W^c$ inherited from the weak equivalences $W$ of $\mathcal M$. Let $j:\mathcal M^c\to\mathcal M$ be inclusion. A functorial factorization of the initial maps as cofibrations followed by trivial fibrations gives $Q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^c$ and a natural trivial fibration $\epsilon:jQ\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$. Then $Q$ preserves weak equivalences, and the induced functors
$$j_\infty:N(\mathcal M^c)[(W^c)^{-1}]\rightleftarrows N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]:Q_\infty$$
are inverse equivalences. The natural transformations induced by $\epsilon$ and its restriction to $\mathcal M^c$ give equivalences $j_\infty Q_\infty\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $Q_\infty j_\infty\simeq\mathrm{id}$ in the corresponding coherent functor categories. In particular these comparisons are natural on coherent diagrams and their transformations, rather than only on homotopy categories.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; functorial-cofibrant-replacement comparison Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent-localization assertion.

proof.text: Factor $\varnothing\to X$ functorially as $\varnothing\to jQX\xrightarrow{\epsilon_X}X$, with the first map a cofibration and the second a trivial fibration, using the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Thus $QX$ is cofibrant. Applying the chosen functorial factorization to the square induced by $f:X\to Y$ gives $Qf:QX\to QY$ and $\epsilon_Yj(Qf)=f\epsilon_X$. Identities and composition are respected because the factorization is functorial. This constructs $Q$ and the natural transformation $\epsilon$ with the stated components.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; explicit agent expansion using the full localization universal property.

proof.text: If $f:X\to Y$ is a weak equivalence, both $f\epsilon_X$ and $\epsilon_Y$ are weak equivalences. The naturality equation from Step 1 and two-out-of-three, part of the model-category axioms in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], imply $j(Qf)\in W$. By the definition of $W^c$, this says $Qf\in W^c$. Inclusion $j$ preserves weak equivalences by the same definition. For a cofibrant object $A$, both $QjA$ and $A$ lie in the full subcategory $\mathcal M^c$, so $\epsilon_{jA}$ is a morphism there and belongs to $W^c$. Its naturality equation is also an equation there, since inclusion is fully faithful. Hence restriction of $\epsilon$ is a natural transformation $\epsilon^c:Qj\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M^c}$.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; explicit agent expansion using the full localization universal property.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]$ and $\mathcal A=N(\mathcal M^c)[(W^c)^{-1}]$, and let $q:N(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal C$ and $q_c:N(\mathcal M^c)\to\mathcal A$ be localization maps. The weak equivalences form systems on the ordinary nerves: isomorphisms are weak equivalences, composition follows from two-out-of-three, and homotopy of arrows of an ordinary nerve identifies equal arrows. Step 2 implies that $qNj$ inverts $W^c$ and $q_cNQ$ inverts $W$. Apply the full functor-category universal property of [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] to obtain $j_\infty:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $Q_\infty:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ with $j_\infty q_c\simeq qNj$ and $Q_\infty q\simeq q_cNQ$. Substituting these comparisons gives $(j_\infty Q_\infty)q\simeq qN(jQ)$ and $(Q_\infty j_\infty)q_c\simeq q_cN(Qj)$.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; explicit agent expansion using the full localization universal property.

proof.text: The nerves of $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon^c$, followed respectively by $q$ and $q_c$, give coherent transformations $qN(jQ)\to q$ and $q_cN(Qj)\to q_c$. Every component is an equivalence because the localization maps invert $W$ and $W^c$. By the component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], these are equivalences in the respective coherent functor categories. Their endpoints invert the relevant weak equivalences by Step 2, so they lie in the full subcategories occurring in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Fullness also puts their inverses and inverse homotopies in those subcategories. Under the equivalences of functor categories supplied by that node, and the comparisons of Step 3, they therefore give $\alpha:j_\infty Q_\infty\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $\beta:Q_\infty j_\infty\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$. In particular $j_\infty$ and $Q_\infty$ are inverse equivalences; these are precisely the transformations descended from the specified replacement maps.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; explicit agent expansion using the full localization universal property.

proof.text: For any simplicial diagram shape $K$ in the enlarged universe, postcomposition gives $\operatorname{Fun}(K,j_\infty)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q_\infty)$. Whiskering $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with each $K$-diagram gives their two composite-to-identity comparisons. At a vertex $k$ of a diagram $D$ the comparison is $\alpha_{D(k)}$ or $\beta_{D(k)}$, an equivalence. The component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes each comparison an equivalence in the diagram quasicategory. These comparisons are natural in $D$: a transformation of $K$-diagrams is a map $K\times\Delta^1$ into the target, and its naturality prism is obtained simply by composing this map with the coherent transformation $\alpha$ or $\beta$; the same composition on $K\times\Delta^n$ supplies every higher compatibility. Thus the comparison acts on coherent diagrams and all their transformations. This proves the final clause without replacing a functor category by its homotopy category.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; explicit agent expansion using the full localization universal property.
